title: Decoupling Order Processing for Artisan Marketplace
business: An online artisan marketplace where independent creators list unique, handcrafted goods for global buyers.
problem: During high-traffic seasonal sales events, the monolithic order-processing service frequently crashes because it cannot handle the sudden spike in concurrent database write requests, leading to lost orders and frustrated customers.
solution: By implementing Amazon SQS, the marketplace decouples the front-end order submission from the back-end fulfillment logic. When a customer places an order, the web application sends a message to an SQS queue instead of attempting a direct database write. A separate worker service polls the queue to process orders at a sustainable rate, ensuring the system remains responsive even when order volume exceeds the immediate processing capacity of the database.
steps: Provision an SQS queue configured to hold order data payloads.
Update the order submission API to transmit order details as a message to the SQS queue.
Develop a worker application that polls the queue for new messages.
Implement logic in the worker to parse the message and execute the database write operation.
Configure the worker to delete the message from the queue only after successful database persistence.
outcome: The marketplace achieves increased system resilience, as order submissions are successfully buffered during traffic surges, preventing service outages and ensuring no order data is discarded.
limitation: A primary limitation is the potential for message latency, as the decoupling introduces a delay between order placement and fulfillment. This can be monitored by checking the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric to ensure the worker service is keeping pace with the incoming message rate.

questions.question: In Decoupling Order Processing for Artisan Marketplace, how does SQS solve the problem of service crashes?
options: By increasing the database write speed directly.
By buffering order messages to allow for sustainable processing rates.
By eliminating the need for a database entirely.
By forcing customers to wait until the database is ready.
questions.explanation: The solution explains that SQS acts as a buffer between the front-end and back-end, allowing the system to handle spikes without overwhelming the database.
questions.evidence: A separate worker service polls the queue to process orders at a sustainable rate, ensuring the system remains responsive even when order volume exceeds the immediate processing capacity of the database.

questions.question: In Decoupling Order Processing for Artisan Marketplace, what is a key limitation of the implementation?
options: The system cannot handle more than ten orders per hour.
The database will always crash regardless of the queue.
The introduction of message latency between order placement and fulfillment.
The queue requires manual deletion of every message by the customer.
questions.explanation: The limitation section explicitly identifies that decoupling introduces a delay in processing, which is a trade-off for system stability.
questions.evidence: A primary limitation is the potential for message latency, as the decoupling introduces a delay between order placement and fulfillment.
